findings.text: `root_path` is interpolated into the regex without `re.escape`. A root_path containing metacharacters, such as `/app(v1` or `/a+b`, raises `re.error` or matches the wrong text, so every request under that mount fails or is routed wrongly.

The strip is a plain string-prefix match with no path-segment boundary check. With root_path `/api` and path `/apifoo/x`, it returns `foo/x`, which has no leading slash and wrongly matches routes. An empty root_path is fine, but a root_path with a trailing slash, such as `/api/`, strips the slash and leaves a path that doesn't start with `/`.
